lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is neighbours and community. And I have a new neighbour — a piano player.
[laugh] Oh no. When does he play?
She. At eleven at night! Every night. The same song.
Did you talk to her?
Not yet. In England we have a saying: keep yourself to yourself. Lots of people don't even know their neighbours' names.
That's so different from here. I grew up in an old building with a big courtyard in the middle. Everybody knew everybody.
What was it like?
The kids played in the courtyard all day, and the grandmothers sat on benches and watched. If a child fell, ten people ran to help.
So the whole neighbourhood helped to look after the children.
Exactly. And if someone cooked plov, a plate went to the neighbours. And you never gave the plate back empty — always with something sweet on it.
I love that. That's real community.
And you, Sam? Do you get along with anyone in your building?
Actually, yes — an old man on the ground floor, Mr Aliyev. Last month my heating stopped working, and my landlord didn't answer for a week.
A week? In November?
Yes! Mr Aliyev came up with a heater and his toolbox, and he fixed it in twenty minutes. He just wanted to lend a hand.
That's so kind. Did you thank him?
I bought him a box of chocolates. Now he invites me for tea every Sunday.
See? Maybe you can try the same with the piano player.
Tea and a polite question? "Do you know any other songs?"
[laugh] Perfect. Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: do you know your neighbours — and what would make your street a friendlier place?
Mine: no piano after ten. See you next time!
Bye for now!
